data.body:
## RE-TRIAGE against the refined bar (accurate-fit-to-scenario-set, not narrowness)

Applied the sharpened standard to every mapping. Net effect: **most findings collapse to `ready-to-fix` with one existing broad-accurate code (`command_failed`)** — no new vocabulary — and several previously-noted "lossy" items are re-confirmed as ACCEPTABLE (accurate-but-broad), not findings.

### The single unifying correction (covers 5f96, 7d47, fbc0, and 73d8/551b)
Narrow every `llm_unavailable` producer so it fires **only for `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError`** — whose scenario set (extra absent, credentials missing/invalid, provider unreachable/rate-limited/refused) accurately fits the name. Every other `LLMError` subclass → **`command_failed`** (existing, broad, honest: "an unclassified rebar command failure"), which makes no false cause claim for input rejections, tool-loop/budget self-stops, context-window, output defects, or workflow/expression faults. This is discriminating by exception TYPE, not by phase — which is why it also dissolves the dbca-AC3 execute-time tension in 73d8 (a real execute-time outage is an `LLMUnavailableError` and stays `llm_unavailable`).

### Re-tags applied
- **7d47** (render_workflow) escalate → **ready-to-fix** (target `command_failed`).
- **fbc0** (_structured_llm_failure) escalate → **ready-to-fix** (narrow to `LLMUnavailableError`, else `command_failed`).
- **5f96** stays **ready-to-fix** (the root branch-6 change; recommendation sharpened to `command_failed`, explicitly NOT split into narrow codes).
- **0aee** stays **ready-to-fix** — reclassified: NOT a misleading/ambiguous mapping, it is a vocabulary-registration gap (emitted code ∉ KNOWN_ERROR_CODES). Fix = add it to the frozenset.
- **f75f** stays **escalate** — a genuine AMBIGUOUS finding (`coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean implies provider-down but its scenario set includes input-rejection). No existing broad-accurate CODE swap fixes a named boolean consumed by 3 readers → contract decision.

### Re-confirmed ACCEPTABLE (accurate-but-broad — NOT findings under the refined bar)
- **branch 7 `command_failed` fallback** — honestly "an unclassified failure"; that is exactly what the branch catches. Accurate-but-broad.
- **`NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` fallback (failure.py)** — honestly "unclassified — inspect the diagnostic." Accurate-but-broad.
- **missing-[agents]-extra → NEEDS_INVESTIGATION** — the classifier cannot import the typed arms without the extra, so "unclassified" is an honest read; deliberate totality guarantee. Not a finding.
- **deps `"not found" in message ? ticket_not_found : deps_failed`** — even on a sniff misfire it lands on `deps_failed` ("the deps command failed"), a broad-accurate code, never a wrong specific cause. Fragile but not misleading. Not a finding (note-only).
- **explain_criterion unknown-kind → command_failed** — honest broad fallback. Accurate.
- **exit codes / reconciler dispositions** — accurate.

### One borderline AMBIGUOUS, deferred (not a new ticket)
- **`config_unreadable` for a malformed-but-readable config** (ConfigError branch): "unreadable" implies an I/O read failure, but the scenario set includes "read fine, failed schema validation." Mildly under-fits. It is a DELIBERATE operator ruling (39f8-ae7c) and low-value, so recording it here rather than filing; revisit only if a broader-accurate name (e.g. `config_invalid`) is wanted.

### Final tallies (post-re-triage)
- MISLEADING (correctable via existing broad-accurate `command_failed`, ready-to-fix): the `llm_unavailable` class at 3 code sites → 5f96, 7d47, fbc0 (+ the pre-existing 73d8/551b, which the same one-line change resolves toward `command_failed`).
- AMBIGUOUS needing a contract decision (escalate): 1 → f75f.
- Vocabulary-registration gap (ready-to-fix): 1 → 0aee.
- Accurate-but-broad, NOT findings: branch-7/NEEDS_INVESTIGATION/missing-extra/deps-sniff/criterion-fallback/exit-codes.
- Borderline deferred: config_unreadable(malformed).

**Prevention recommendation is unchanged and stronger under this bar:** the exhaustive `LLMError` subclass→code contract test should assert each subclass maps to an accurate-fit code (genuine availability types → `llm_unavailable`; all others → `command_failed` or a deliberately-declared finer code), so a new subclass cannot silently inherit the misleading `llm_unavailable`.
